newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telecinco considers bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telecinco considers bourse listing.

text.p: Spanish television broadcaster Gestevision Telecinco Sa is considering the possibility of a listing on the bourse, but, for the time being, the law on private television prohibits it, a top official of the group told Reuters.

"We fully intend to list on the bourse. But we find ourselves limited by the law on private television which demands an administrative procedure before allowing changes in the title of the shares and prohibits the company from listing," deputy manager for administration and financial head Jose Luis Puche told Reuters.
Financial daily Expansion reported on Monday that Telecinco had asked the Ministry of Development to change the private television law, so it could list its shares.
Puche said it had talked to the Ministry about the matter, but he gave no details.
The Ministry could not confirm whether Telecinco had presented an official request.

Telecinco belongs 25 percent to the Kirch group, 25 percent to Mediaset, 25 percent to Sotelcin, 10 percent to Prensa Espanola, 13 percent to the International Bank of Luxembourg and two percent in minority shareholders hands.
Puche confirmed that for the first time Telecinco planned to pay a dividend but he gave no details about the amount.
